title: A month of promises, still tomorrow
odia:
ଦେବୁ ଦେବୁ ବୋଲି ପୂରିଲା ମାସେ
ଆହୁରି ବୋଲୁଚୁ କାଲିକି ଆ’ସେ।
literal_meaning: A month has passed with you saying you will give; still you say, “Come tomorrow.”
meaning_odia: ଦେବୁ ବୋଲି ବାରମ୍ବାର କହିବାରେ ମାସେ ବିତିଗଲା, ତଥାପି କାଲି ଆସିବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ପୂରଣ ନହୋଇ ଦିନ ଗଡ଼ିଚାଲିବା ପ୍ରତି ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ଅସନ୍ତୋଷ ଏଥିରେ ପ୍ରକାଶ ପାଉଛି। କଣ ଦେବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଇଥିଲା, ମୂଳ ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ।
explanation: Repeated assurances have turned into a month of waiting, yet the answer remains “tomorrow.” The complaint is about a promise continually pushed ahead instead of fulfilled. The verse leaves the promised thing unnamed, so its force can extend beyond any one kind of transaction.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone has repeatedly promised to provide material for a shared project. After weeks of being asked to return the next day, the waiting colleague recalls this saying.
cultural_context: The repeated ଦେବୁ makes the assurance sound habitual. A whole month in the first line is set against one more tomorrow in the second, giving the delay its sharpness.

english_summary: Repeated promises leave the waiting person with another tomorrow.
